title: HLD Thinking
subtitle: Constraints first: a component earns its place by answering a force
motto: Don't start with components. Start with forces.
keyInsight: Drawing the usual four boxes leaves real needs unanswered and boxes unexplained, and drawing everything adds boxes nothing asked for, so each component must trace back to a constraint.

decisions.title: Compare two opposite mistakes
decisions.description: The failure frame draws a habit-driven template and the trade-off frame draws every component, so both under-building and over-building are measured against the justified set.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only the missing components would suggest more boxes are always safer.

decisions.title: Explicit rules instead of a lookup of 'best practice'
decisions.description: Each component is a one-line predicate on the constraints, so changing one slider visibly changes which boxes are justified.
decisions.alternatives: A fixed reference architecture would hide the link between force and component.
